title: Joyal localization is Cat-infinity
statement: Use simplicial sets, quasicategories, categorical equivalences and universes of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure], homotopy coherent localizations in the sense of [def-coef-coherent-localization-interface], simplicial categories, locally Kan replacement and the homotopy coherent nerve of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison], and the infinity category $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$ of small quasicategories of [lem-coef-cat-infinity-colimits-cartesian-closure]. Let $W_{\mathrm J}$ be the class of categorical equivalences between small simplicial sets, and let $q:N(\mathsf{sSet})\to\mathcal L$ be a homotopy coherent localization of the ordinary category of small simplicial sets at $W_{\mathrm J}$ (for instance the homotopy coherent nerve of a locally Kan replacement of its hammock localization). Then there is an equivalence of infinity categories $\Phi:\mathcal L\simeq\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$ together with equivalences $\Phi(q(Q))\simeq Q$ for every small quasicategory $Q$, natural in simplicial maps between quasicategories, so that $\Phi q$ restricted to quasicategories is the inclusion of small quasicategories into $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$. The equivalence is induced by the Joyal--Bergner coherent-nerve Quillen equivalence and the derived coherent nerve, and concerns the ordinary Joyal model with its cartesian mapping objects, with no Kan-enrichment hypothesis. It holds in every universe and is compatible with enlarging the universe.

source.place: Theorem 2.2.5.1, Corollary 2.2.5.4 and Proposition 2.2.5.8 (Joyal model and coherent-nerve comparison); online PDF, archival source WANTED.

proof.text: By [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure], in each universe simplicial sets carry the Joyal model structure whose cofibrations are degreewise injective maps and whose weak equivalences are exactly the categorical equivalences used to define $W_{\mathrm J}$; its fibrant objects are exactly the quasicategories. Thus the class inverted in the statement is the weak-equivalence class of the ordinary Joyal model, and the objects called quasicategories are its fibrant objects.

source.place: Theorem 2.2.5.1, Lemma 2.2.5.2 and Proposition 2.2.5.8; online PDF, archival source WANTED

proof.text: The coherent-nerve comparison [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison] gives the adjunction $\mathfrak C\dashv N_{\mathrm{hc}}$ as a Quillen equivalence from the Joyal model to the Bergner model. Its derived coherent nerve identifies the resulting homotopy theory of simplicial categories with the infinity category $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$ of small quasicategories, and the comparison is natural for simplicial functors. Consequently the Joyal homotopy theory has the claimed quasicategorical presentation.

source.place: Theorem 2.2.5.1, Corollary 2.2.5.4 and Proposition 2.2.5.8; online PDF, archival source WANTED

proof.text: For the relative category of small simplicial sets and $W_{\mathrm J}$, [lem-coef-hammock-infinity-localization] constructs a locally Kan replacement of the hammock localization and its homotopy coherent nerve $\mathcal L$, together with the map $q:N(\mathsf{sSet})\to\mathcal L$. The node states that this map is a universal infinity localization: precomposition identifies functors out of $\mathcal L$ with the full infinity subcategory of functors out of $N(\mathsf{sSet})$ that invert $W_{\mathrm J}$.

source.place: Theorem 2.2.5.1 and Proposition 2.2.5.8; hammock localization construction, online source WANTED

proof.text: Let $q_{\mathrm J}:N(\mathsf{sSet})\to\mathcal L_{\mathrm J}$ be the coherent localization supplied by the Joyal model structure. The derived-adjunction result applied to the Quillen equivalence of Step 2 gives an equivalence between the coherent localizations of the Joyal and Bergner model categories, with the derived unit and counit as coherent natural transformations. Composing this equivalence with the derived coherent nerve of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison] identifies $\mathcal L_{\mathrm J}$ with $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$. The hammock localization $q_H:N(\mathsf{sSet})\to\mathcal L_H$ of Step 3 has the same universal property as $q_{\mathrm J}$, so [lem-coef-system-localization-universal] gives an equivalence $u:\mathcal L_H\simeq\mathcal L_{\mathrm J}$ with $u q_H\simeq q_{\mathrm J}$. For a quasicategory $Q$, the derived unit is $\eta_Q:Q\to N_{\mathrm{hc}}R\mathfrak C[Q]$; the Quillen-equivalence criterion makes it a Joyal weak equivalence. Both ends are quasicategories, and [lem-coef-joyal-quasicategory-characterizations] turns this weak equivalence into a simplicial quasi-inverse and coherent inverse transformations, hence an equivalence in $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$.

source.place: Theorem 2.2.5.1, Corollary 2.2.5.4 and Proposition 2.2.5.8; derived localization and Quillen-equivalence comparison

proof.text: Now let $q:N(\mathsf{sSet})\to\mathcal L$ be the arbitrary localization in the statement. Since both $q$ and $q_H$ invert exactly $W_{\mathrm J}$ and satisfy the full coherent functor-category universal property, factorization gives functors $F:\mathcal L\to\mathcal L_H$ and $G:\mathcal L_H\to\mathcal L$ with specified equivalences $Fq\simeq q_H$ and $Gq_H\simeq q$. The equivalence of restriction functor categories in [lem-coef-system-localization-universal], applied to the two composites, supplies $GF\simeq\mathrm{id}$ and $FG\simeq\mathrm{id}$. Define $\Phi=(\text{the comparison }\mathcal L_H\simeq\mathrm{Cat}_\infty)\circ F$. The derived-unit equivalences of Step 4 and the equivalence $Fq\simeq q_H$ give $\Phi(q(Q))\simeq Q$. If $f:Q\to Q'$ is a simplicial map between quasicategories, functoriality of $R$, naturality of the adjunction unit, and the naturality of the coherent-nerve comparison for the simplicial functor $\mathfrak C[f]$ identify the resulting square with $f$; therefore these equivalences are natural in simplicial maps. Every construction is made in a chosen universe, and the universe clauses in the three cited nodes are preserved under enlargement.

Step 4: the derived-adjunction node's hypotheses hold. Every object is Joyal-cofibrant. R𝔠[Q] is locally Kan, hence Bergner-fibrant, since the lifting condition over the terminal category is vacuous. 𝔠[Q]→R𝔠[Q] is a Dwyer–Kan equivalence. So by the Quillen-equivalence criterion η_Q: Q→N_hc R𝔠[Q] is a Joyal weak equivalence. Both ends are quasicategories, so characterization (2) makes η_Q an equivalence in Cat_∞. The localization-uniqueness node applies because W_J contains the isomorphisms. Step 5 handles an arbitrary q: F and G come from the two universal properties, and full faithfulness of restriction gives GF≃id and FG≃id. Naturality follows from functoriality of R, strict naturality of the unit and the coherent-nerve node's naturality for 𝔠[f]. Edge cases checked: ∅, Δ⁰, identity maps, universe enlargement.
